02 .  This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode) This writ petition has been filed by the Ansupa Farmers Union, Banki through its Secretary Alok Ranjan Beura as petitioner No.1, Satrughna Rout as petitioner No.2 and Jitendera Kumar Khatua as petitioner No.3, Panchanan Mohanty as Petitioner no.4 and Bhubanananda Panda as petitioner No.5 with a prayer for following directions;-
"In this above premises, it is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to:-
Ansupa Farmers Union vs State Of Odisha on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160589710/
1 a. Call for the records pertaining to the matter under challenge and issue a rule nisi,
directing the opposite parties to show cause as to why the relief sought by the petitioners should not be granted and if the opposite parties failure to show cause or show insufficient cause;
b. Issue an appropriate writ, order(s) or direction(s), more particularly a Writ in the nature of Mandamus directing the Opposite Parties to initiate the Land Acquisition proceedings for the acquired farmlands under Section-11 & 15 of Right to Fair Compensation, Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013; and c. Issue an appropriate writ, order(s) or direction(s), more particularly a writ in the nature of Mandamus directing the Opposite Parties to compensate the affected farmer members of the petitioners immediately and adequately in accordance with the Right to Fair Compensation, Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 taking all the relevant parameters into consideration as mandated under Section-28 and 30 of the said Act; and d. Issue an appropriate writ, order(s) or direction(s), directing the Opposite Parties to provide interest on entire amount of compensation including solatium as per Section-80 to the affected farmer members of the petitioners for the whole period for which the State Government was in illegal possession over their land; and e. Pass such further or other orders as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper under the circumstances of the case."

In this writ petition it is stated in paragraph No.2 that petitioner No.1 is an unregistered association of affected farmers formed under Article 19 (1) (c) of the Constitution of India and is competent to pursue the litigation on behalf of the affected land owners being the large body of the persons with common grievances.

Learned counsel for the petitioners placing reliance on the decisions of Dalco Engineering Pvt. Ltd.
vs. Satish Prabhakar Padhye & Ors. (2010) 4 SCC 378 so also Umesh Chand Vinod Kumar & Ors.

sentences.text:
Vs.
Krishi Utpadan Mandi Samiti, Bharthana & Anr.
SCC OnLine Allhabad 638 submitted that at the instance of these 5 petitioners the writ petition is maintainable but we are not satisfied with such submissions.
An unregistered Association has filed the writ petition.
There is no document relating to the institution of the members of the Association or framing of any bye- laws.
The resolution annexed to the writ petition does not contain the signatures of the members except that of the President and Secretary.
These facts are absolutely necessary for inferring that the petitioner No.1 is espousing the cause of non-payment of compensation amount for the acquisition of land duly authorized by its members.
Neither any document nor pleadings are available on record reflecting the intention of the so- called members and authorization to the petitioner No.1.
We are therefore of the view that the petitioner No.1 Association does not have a valid existence so as to maintain this petition.
This writ petition is not maintainable at the instance of petitioner No.1.

sentences.text: It is up to the farmers who have been allegedly affected due to the non-receipt of the compensation amount in spite of acquisition of land, to raise their grievance in the appropriate forum.

It appears that one legal notice has been served vide Annexure-6 to the Additional Chief Secretary,
Revenue & Disaster Management Dept., Additional Chief Secretary, Department of Forest,
Envioronment & Climate Change, Collector & District Magistrate, Cuttack, Chief Executive, Chilika Development Authority and from Annexure-5 it appears that a grievance has been registered in the Chief Minister Grievance cell on 02.01.2023.
It is open to the petitioners to pursue such grievance if so advised.
